name: French Onion Grilled Cheese
description: French onion soup as a sandwich: onions caramelized slowly and deglazed with sherry and beef stock until jammy, layered with nutty Gruyère between buttery sourdough, griddled with a frico-crisp Parmesan crust. Serves 2.

ingredients.text: 2 large yellow onions (about 500 g), thinly sliced
ingredients.item: large yellow onions (about 500 g), thinly sliced

ingredients.text: 60 ml dry sherry or dry white wine
ingredients.item: dry sherry or dry white wine

steps.text: Melt 2 tbsp butter (for the onions) in a wide skillet over medium. Add 2 large yellow onions (about 500 g), thinly sliced and 1/4 tsp salt and cook 10 minutes, stirring, until soft. Lower the heat to medium-low and cook 35 minutes more, stirring every few minutes and scraping the browned bits, until deep amber and jammy. Add a splash of water if they start to catch.

Add 1/2 tsp fresh thyme leaves and 60 ml dry sherry or dry white wine and scrape the pan as it bubbles away, about 1 minute. Add 120 ml beef stock and 1/2 tsp Worcestershire sauce and simmer 4 minutes, until almost dry. Season with 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Spread 2 tbsp softened butter (for the bread) on one side of each slice of 4 slices sourdough bread, 1.5 cm thick and sprinkle 20 g Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated over the butter, pressing it in.
Flip two slices over and top each with a quarter of 150 g Gruyère, grated, half the onions and another quarter of the cheese. Close with the other slices, Parmesan side out.
Cook in a skillet over medium-low, covered, for 4 minutes per side, until the crust is deep golden and the cheese has melted. Rest 1 minute, then cut.

notes: Caramelizing takes time: 45 minutes is not padding. The onions keep for a week in the fridge, so make a double batch. Warm extra beef stock with a splash of sherry for dipping, like a soup and sandwich in one.
